content:
incident-bot: Pager — GEO probe bounce detected: health-checks toggling across us-east <-> us-west <-> eu for routing group 'gen-1'. breach_count=6 in 5m. auto-fallback triggered repeatedly. @maya (oncall) please investigate

maya (oncall): on it. landing in call room. first glance: spikes in probe failrates, looks like two probes disagreeing on health window.

sam (runtime): joining. logs show the routing policy 'smart-fallback-v2' dropped the cool-down to 10s earlier today (from 60s) as part of perf test. that could explain oscillation.

leo (network): FYI there's a transient network blip between us-east and us-west reported by cloud provider at 02:03 UTC — but the cloud metric spike is small and not enough to OOS instances.

maya (oncall): customer-facing impact? jordan?

jordan (support): getting multiple alerts from a handful of tenants — roughly 8% of requests saw elevated latency and ~3% 5xx on retries. major customers A and C opened cases.

sam (runtime): root cause hypothesis: aggressive fallback cooldown + slightly noisy health-check TTL = ping-pong. routing policy immediately falls back to next region, which then sees short-lived probe failure and falls back again.

maya (oncall): mitigation plan — immediate and quick: 1) disable auto-fallback for gen-1 route (to stop churn) 2) raise probe cooldown to 45s 3) pin active model variant to stable-1 for affected routes to avoid model-variant mismatch during handoff.

leo (network): can we throttle fallback by changing routing policy weights instead of disable? we can, but disable is fastest.

maya (oncall): doing disable now. runbook command: 
```bash
# disable auto fallback for routing group gen-1
redwoodctl routing set --group gen-1 --auto-fallback false --context production
```

ops-bot: Command accepted. change request id cr-20260315-423 applied by maya.

sam (runtime): increasing health_decay and probe cooldown in the routing policy: applying patch.
```yaml
routing_policy: smart-fallback-v2
changes:
  health_decay: 45s
  probe_cooldown: 45s
  fallback_threshold: 0.7
```

ops-bot: Patch rolled to 3 control-plane nodes (canary), will roll to all in 30s unless rollback.

jordan (support): customers A & C patched notification: we let them know mitigation in progress. low-severity status page update queued.

maya (oncall): monitoring for 2m. watching per-region request counts, error rates, and model-variant drift. sam, confirm model-variant pin deployed?

sam (runtime): pinned stable-1 on prod route gen-1: 
```bash
redwoodctl model pin --route gen-1 --model stable-1 --duration 1h
```
ops-bot: pin applied.

maya (oncall): error rates dropping — good. latency normalizing. customer incidents still open but no new alerts.

leo (network): cloud provider alert cleared at 02:07 UTC. but the policy change clearly stopped the oscillation.

sam (runtime): postmortem action items: 1) revert the perf test that reduced cooldown; 2) add a safety check in smart-fallback to require two consecutive probe failures across two regions before fallback; 3) add a canary flag for cooldown changes that prevents immediate rollout to all regions.

maya (oncall): assigning actions: sam -> revert perf test + add safety check; leo -> validate cloud provider metrics correlation and add provider flakiness telemetry to routing decision; jordan -> follow up with affected customers with timeline; i'll own post-incident doc + SLA impact calc.

jordan (support): note for customer comms: affected window ~02:03–02:10 UTC, approx 7m. approx 8% of requests in gen-1 experienced latency spike, 3% 5xx on retry.

maya (oncall): handoff: i'm oncall for another 1.5h and will watch. if things reoccur, page SRE rotation. filing incident ticket.

ops-bot: Incident ticket INC-20260315-94 created and linked: https://redwood/incidents/INC-20260315-94

sam (runtime): quick thing — we saw a couple of requests that briefly hit an older quantized variant due to cache invalidation during the flips. any noted inference-quality regressions? jordan?

jordan (support): customers reported a small uptick in malformed JSON outputs for one tenant — investigating. looks limited.

maya (oncall): ok. follow-ups captured. good job team. keeping this thread open for final postmortem notes. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident severity adjusted to SEV2 -> reduced after mitigation.
